proof_summary: For \(k\ge 60\), set \(n=2k+1\); if \(4k+2\) had no representation as a sum of two primes, every matrix entry would vanish, since its two candidate primes \(n+i-j\) and \(n+j-i\) sum to \(2n=4k+2\), forcing the determinant to be zero and contradicting the hypothesis. The cases \(1\le k<60\) are discharged by explicit prime pairs.
